findings: The production diff contains none of the fresh or prior review labels and no held-out entity/package names.
The production diff introduces no fixture or golden reads, embedded source/SVG data, source-line equality branch, coordinate/dimension branch, per-count ladder, or layout constant.

The exactly-one threshold is mechanism-shaped and directly supported by Plasma.countByName(name) == 1. The union of entity and package canonical paths correctly addresses group participation for the non-null-separator branch.
The explicit CurrentContext versus ReuseUnique enum correctly repairs the prior ordinary-declaration overgeneralization across class, enum, and interface controls.

The implementation is nevertheless incomplete against its own durable response: review-5-response.md says namespaceSeparator none retains Java's separate first-name behavior, but resolve_quark_path calls unique_quark_path_named in that branch.

Because entity_by_path and package_by_path are HashMaps and unique_quark_path_named collects into a HashSet, the new representation does not retain the creation order required by Plasma.firstWithName.

findings.title: namespaceSeparator none implements uniqueness instead of first-created reuse
evidence: review6_namespace_none_duplicate_first_match.puml is valid Java syntax and its SVG is not an error page.
Java reuses SepNoneAlpha.EchoToken after two EchoToken quarks exist and creates no root EchoToken.
Rust creates root EchoToken at declaration source line 8.
CucaDiagram.quarkInContextSafe's sep == null branch calls firstWithName without consulting reuseExistingChild or countByName.
Rust resolve_quark_path's namespace_sep.is_none branch calls unique_quark_path_named and therefore implements the wrong predicate.
The discrepancy was named in the pre-implementation review-5 response, so this is an omitted part of the documented model rather than a newly inferred requirement.

findings.title: Unique remote mixed reuse leaves an extra misqualified package cluster
evidence: review6_unique_mixed_reuses_remote_class.puml is valid Java syntax and its SVG is not an error page.
Java and Rust both reuse BridgeClasses.TransitBridge, proving the unique leaf lookup itself fires.
Java emits only BridgeClasses as a cluster because BridgeActors owns no rendered leaf after reuse.
Rust emits an extra cluster qualified as BridgeClasses.BridgeActors at declaration source line 5.
This is parser-owned group identity/metadata, not renderer geometry.
